worked: **What didn't (the recurring blind spot):** twice the UI work drifted from the product's core: v2 abandoned the kanban class for a "prettier" ledger, and labels/sub-items were missing from every version because the design doc never specified card anatomy. Root: optimizing the frontend-design distinctiveness brief instead of the named product class. The user's frustration ("looks ass", "not there", "did you lose track of the core goal") is the signal — for a thing named after a known artifact class, the class anatomy IS the spec, and every redesign OPTION must preserve it. The board still isn't satisfying.

**Gotchas:** (a) a mutation test that stays GREEN means the fix STRUCTURE is the bug — a belt-and-braces pre-lock check masked the throw-based lock release and had to be REMOVED to make the guard pinnable. (b) Bun `process.exit()` skips `finally` even nested inside try — the whole lock-leak class. (c) `2>/dev/null` on a probe converts "helper broken" into a misleading "server down" diagnosis. (d) the subagent-output guard needs the literal persist-contract phrasing (named path + who writes).

**Notes for future agents:** kanban verbs now include show/drop/unregister/--json; `agent-experience-actions.md` is the standing regression test (re-run after any kanban change). PLAN.md carries full dispositions. The board is a column kanban in ink/gold; the user is not yet happy with the look — the UI narrowing page is the disciplined path, do NOT redesign freehand.
